verdicts.recommendation: C6.1 compare_runs de-identified ledger, fire_and_forget behind ENABLE_COMPARE_RUN_LEDGER
verdicts.reason: fire_and_forget does not mean off-loop. run_db calls .execute() inline while ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is OFF, and prod keeps it OFF. So each ledger insert, a large JSONB row, blocks the single uvicorn loop for one RTT (285 ms p50 insert, 381 ms read). comparison_id exists only after persist_comparison, so the write has to chain after it. The re-compare flag needs an extra query_hash read, which still needs user linkage.
verdicts.fix: Write compare_runs as ONE insert chained after persist_comparison inside the existing track_after_persist task (or at the delivery exit for anonymous runs). Compute the re-compare flag in the nightly job, not per request. Enable it only after ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is canaried, or accept and measure about 300 ms of loop stall per compare.

verdicts.recommendation: C6.2 Batch Haiku judge plus Sonnet escalation plus grounded web_search checks
verdicts.reason: $0.0004 assumes 6K input and 0.4K output. A real evidence payload for two products is unmeasured and probably 10-20K tokens with the +30% tokenizer, and Haiku/Sonnet 5.5 adaptive thinking bills extra output. Sonnet runs on EVERY Haiku flag with no cap; at a 30% flag rate and 1000/day that is about $10/day. Grounded checks pay $10/1k searches plus search-result tokens, and 'disputes' are uncapped. A Batch result can take up to 24 h, so a chained escalation can lag about 48 h.

verdicts.recommendation: C6.4 Q1 identity question after 8 s dwell plus rotating Q2
verdicts.reason: Serving cost is negligible: one /feedback insert per answer. But label yield is unmeasured. Q2 is split three ways and gated on a Q1 Yes, so price_correct receives roughly answer-rate x Yes-rate / 3 of compares. At 100/day and a 10% answer rate that is about 2 price labels a day. That starves C6.5's 3-case, 2-device threshold and the Sonnet-on-No trigger. The 8 s dwell figure is unbenchmarked against a 22 s p50 stream.
verdicts.fix: Ship Q1 first and measure the answer rate and the dwell distribution for a week. Then set the Q2 rotation weights (for example price-heavy for fragrances) and the C6.5 thresholds from the measured label volume.

verdicts.recommendation: C6.5 nightly cron, failure clustering, exemplars, eval proof by A/B and 60-case set
verdicts.reason: The proof plan is not costed. 60 cases x 2 reps = 120 prod-HTTP compares per run, which is about 1.5k Serper credits plus LLM spend at smoke20's 10-15 credits a compare, and they hit the new 3/day per-device quota. An A/B by hash_bucket at 100-300 compares/day needs weeks to clear noise, which conflicts with weekly rotation. Two prefix versions also split the cache, and at under 300/day the 5-min-TTL gaps rarely hit it anyway.

verdicts.recommendation: C6.6 review KB from JSON-LD, partner keys, Trustpilot; delete GPT rating fallback
verdicts.reason: The channel 1 parse is genuinely near-free: price_service already walks the Product node and reads aggregateRating. But coverage is measured at 14.0% (aggregateRating) and 9.3% (reviewBody). Four new tables add per-compare upserts and reads. With offload OFF, a gather of Supabase calls serialises on the loop, so 3 extra reads at a 381 ms p50 add about 1.1 s. Trustpilot is quote-only, with a 24 h refresh. YouTube's quota covers about 49 compares/day, below 300.

verdicts.recommendation: C6.7 single post-approval legal window: Anthropic, consent v3, PostHog, Terms
verdicts.reason: No per-compare token or DB cost. Bundling every change into one window means one consent re-ask instead of two, which minimises the one-time friction of the consent gate. PostHog funnels only, without LLM analytics, stay within the free tier at 1000/day (well under 1M events/month at about 20 events per compare). Its SDK queues off the request path. The 29-day Batch retention figure is not verified locally, but it is a disclosure item, not a cost.
evidence: R12 recommendation (d): one legal unit via U8, re-ask once

new_risks: With ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD OFF in prod, every new Supabase write or read added by C6.1/C6.2/C6.6 (ledger, judgements, ratings, excerpts, claims) blocks the single uvicorn loop for 285-381 ms and serialises supposedly parallel gathers. No recommendation makes the offload canary a precondition.

There is no global LLM spend guard across generation, judge, escalation and grounded checks against the $400 credits. A burst of Haiku flags or user No answers could exhaust credits silently, because Batch spend surfaces only up to 24 h later.

No recommendation exempts the eval and replay harness (smoke20 and the 60-case set over prod HTTP) from the new 3-compares-per-day-per-device quota or from is_synthetic metering, so the proof runs would be blocked or pollute the ledger and feedback stats.

Prompt-cache economics are assumed, not measured. At 100-300 compares/day the start-to-start gap per category prefix is often over 5 min, so cache writes at 1.25x may exceed the reads saved. No digest measured inter-arrival times or cache_read_input_tokens.

Judge input size is unmeasured. A full_response plus product_data evidence bundle for 2 products after the +30% Haiku 5.5 tokenizer could be 2-3x the assumed 6K tokens, and adaptive thinking output is not budgeted in any per-compare cost figure.

Stream-path early disconnects. The ledger and judgement writes have to fire in the stream finally block. Without ENABLE_PREVERDICT_DISCONNECT_ABORT, the verdict tail is still paid for abandoned compares, and no recommendation says whether abandoned runs are judged (paid) or skipped.
